thread:
sam_payments: Heads-up — KioskCo reported ~30 autopay failures in the last 2 hours. Root error shows card_declined + acs_challenge_failed. Request id sample: rq_0a1b2c3d. Merchant says it only affects EU B2B cards when VAT=applied.

anya_support: Oof. Any screenshots from the merchant or ACS response body?

sam_payments: Merchant pasted ACS iframe that just shows 'Authentication failed' and closes. From our logs: 
```
2024-10-05T14:12:03Z req=rq_0a1b2c3d status=decline reason=acs_challenge_failed acs_code=NO_CHALLENGE device_fingerprint=fingerprint_mismatch fraud_score=92 route=eu-cluster-1
```

mike_infra: score=92 -> automatic fraud hold. device_fingerprint looks like our JS SDK output. Are they double-sending a merchant fingerprint header? That can cause mismatch with ACS.

olivia_prod: Checking ingress logs for rq_0a1b2c3d... I see the customer-submitted header `X-Merchant-Fingerprint: 7d3f...` and our sdk cookie `rf_fp=3a9b...`. Those differ. ACS expects consistent device id.

anya_support: Is the merchant using an iframe for 3DS or redirect? They mentioned iframe. iframe + third-party cookie/samesite issues often break fingerprint persistence.

sam_payments: They use an embedded iframe for ACS challenge in checkout modal. Browser console shows blocked third-party cookies earlier for some sessions.

payments-bot: alert: autopay-failure-rate for merchant=kioskco > 25% over 1h window.

mike_infra: Repro plan: 1) Try a local autopay with EU test card that triggers challenge. 2) Force our SDK to emit fingerprint via header instead of relying on iframe cookie. 3) Capture ACS flow and debug the fingerprint passed to ACS.

sam_payments: Repro curl I used (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/payments/charge \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"amount": 1990, "currency": "EUR", "customer": {"email":"qa@kiosk.test"}, "payment_method": {"type":"card", "brand":"visa", "last4":"0002"}, "metadata": {"po":"PO-123"}}'
```

olivia_prod: When I replay with our hosted SDK flow in EU region and enable 3DS iframe, the JS fingerprint cookie is set only on top-level for some browsers. If merchant wraps ACS iframe in their own container, ACS sees a different device id.

anya_support: Short-term mitigation for KioskCo: 1) Switch autopay to redirect-based ACS if merchant can. 2) Or have merchant pass the same device_fingerprint header we generate (rf_fp) to the backend so we forward it to ACS.

mike_infra: Also we should lower the fraud hold threshold for autopay routes for legacy merchants while we investigate; but need sign-off from risk. @olivia_prod can you open a risk ticket?

olivia_prod: On it — creating ticket with logs + sample requests. ticket: RISK-5721.

sam_payments: Merchant asked for repro steps we can give their devs. Proposed minimal repro:
1) Use EU test card that requires challenge.
2) Embed ACS iframe in a cross-origin container and block third-party cookies.
3) Send payment through autopay route.
Expected result: ACS challenge fails due to fingerprint mismatch and we mark decline with acs_challenge_failed + fraud_score >= threshold.

anya_support: Can we add a short-term fallback on our side: if acs returns NO_CHALLENGE but we detect fingerprint mismatch + high fraud score, provide a soft-decline reason 'challenge_unavailable' and surface clear retry guidance to merchants?

mike_infra: We can add a mapping in the router quickly to translate acs_code + fingerprint-mismatch -> challenge_unavailable. I'll open a PR for a hotfix with tests. ETA a few hours.

payments-bot: deploy: payments-router v1.12.4 hotfix queued by mike_infra.

sam_payments: Thanks — will tell merchant: try redirect flow or forward our rf_fp header, and we will roll the hotfix.

olivia_prod: Follow-up: I've attached the merchant's screencap to RISK-5721 and asked Risk to approve temporary threshold change.

anya_support: Great. After hotfix, we should ping merchant to test and collect a full HAR of the failed flow if it persists.

sam_payments: Will coordinate. Marking thread for follow-up after deploy. :thumbsup:
